corrections.currentAnswer: According to the applied methodology VM0042 (version 2.1), continuation of pre-project ALM practices is the most plausible baseline scenario
corrections.currentQuote: According to the applied methodology VM0042 (version 2.1), continuation of pre-project ALM practices is the most plausible baseline scenario. Following the methodology guidance, the baseline scenario is determined by producing an annual schedule of activities from the practices applied in each field/farming unit/project activity instance, from a historic look-back period (of at least three years or to include one complete crop-cycle). Baseline emissions/stock changes are then modeled (Quantification Approach 1) or (for SOC stock change only) directly measured in baseline control sites subject to the annual schedule of activities (Quantification Approach 2).

corrections.correctedAnswer: The project screens the VM0042 leakage pathways and concludes that leakage is not applicable because the project does not involve the identified leakage activities
corrections.correctedQuote: Leakage Management According to paragraph 8.4 of VM0042 (version 2.1) , improved ALM projects may result in leakage through: new application of organic fertilizers and soil conditioners from outside the project area (i.e., organic amendments applied in the project from outside of the project area, that were not previously applied in the historical look-back period); productivity declines; displacement of livestock outside of the project boundary; and/or diversion of biomass residues that were used for bioenergy applications in the baseline scenario. The project does not involve manure treatment, productivity declines, the displacement of livestock outside of the project boundary or diversion of biomass residues that were used for bioenergy applications in the baseline scenario. Thus, it is not applicable to this project.
